sections.COMMENTS:
This composite source straddles the island of Ischia, to the west of the Gulf of Naples. This source is a high-angle, NW-dipping, normal fault perpendicular to the NW-SE trending Tyrrhenian margin of the Campania region.
Historical catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show a concentration of intermediate to damaging earthquakes in the area. In particular, this region has been affected by the 2 February 1828 (Mw 5.6, Casamicciola Terme), 4 March 1881 (Mw 5.4, Isola dâ€™Ischia), and 26 July 1883 (Mw 5.8, Casamicciola Terme) earthquakes.
The location and geometry of the Ischia Source is inferred from geological observations, regional structural trend and earthquake intensity data. Historical seismicity shows that the northern part is the active and seismogenic area of the island of Ischia. A general consensus exists concerning the role of major NE-SW trending, high-angle extensional structures that affect the resurgent block of Ischia.
The main segment of this Source has been associated with the 26 July 1883 earthquake. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenesis in this region, the reader can refer to the Individual Source in this Database. Although the historical catalog report a Mw estimate of 5.8 (Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004), Mw estimates of earthquakes that occur in active volcanic regions may yield further uncertainties - and particularly when no instrumental data are available (as it is clearly the case for this earthquake).
The strike of this Source is based on geological data from various authors, like dip, rake, indicative of pure normal faulting, and minimum and maximum depth. Slip rate was inferred from geological observations in other structures that share the same tectonic regime with this Source.
